Summary

The whole event at a glance, then each day and each race.

Executive summary

Sat 18 Jul

Day: 3 races; wind 263–268°; starts 1–6 s late; upwind 96–101% of target; heel 15–19°; 13 tacks away from the marks: 2 on headers, 6 on lifts; worked the right on 5 of 5 beats (1 beat trended left, 0 right); laylines 4 good / 1 overstood.

  • Race 1 (11:45, 49 min): Start 4 s late, middle, accelerating (+1.6 kt); upwind 5.73 kt (100% of target), heel 18°; downwind 5.83 kt; 7 tacks (33% speed loss), 2 tacks on a header vs 0 on a lift; beats: oscillating (we went right), oscillating (we went right).
  • Race 2 (12:49, 51 min): Start 6 s late, middle, flat (+0.2 kt); upwind 5.75 kt (101% of target), heel 19°; downwind 5.51 kt; 9 tacks (31% speed loss), 0 tacks on a header vs 3 on a lift; beats: oscillating (we went right), trending left 9° (we went right). Flags: 1 layline overstood; 3 tacks on lifts; leg 3: wind went left, we went right.
  • Race 3 (14:05, 25 min): Start 1 s late, middle, slowing (-0.7 kt); upwind 5.45 kt (96% of target), heel 15°; downwind 4.79 kt; 4 tacks (37% speed loss), 0 tacks on a header vs 3 on a lift; beats: oscillating (we went right). Flags: upwind speed 96% of target; 3 tacks on lifts; deep tacks (37% loss).

Facts only; the debrief decides what matters. Targets use the wind given with --tws (or trusted logged wind). Shift calls come from headings.

Debrief

The coaching debrief.

July ODW, Saturday July 18, 2026 (San Diego)

Three windward-leewards in an 8–10 kt westerly around 263–268°, oscillating about ±4°. Starts close to the gun, speed on target, and one clear tactical pattern: we tacked off lifts and kept heading right.

What went well

  • Starts were close to the gun. 4 s, 6 s and 1 s late, all mid-line. Race 1 accelerated well through the gun (+1.6 kt from −5 s to +5 s).
  • Speed on target. 100–101% of the card at 9 kt in races 1 and 2 (96% in the lighter race 3), with heel within 2–3° of target. Much closer to the card than Sunday.
  • Laylines mostly good. Four of five final tacks fetched the mark cleanly. The exception overstood by ~10° (race 2, first beat).

Top 3 to work on

  1. We tacked on lifts, not headers. Of 13 tacks away from the start and marks, 6 were on a lift, only 2 on a header, and 5 had no clear shift. Five of the six left a lifted starboard tack to go onto port. In an oscillating breeze that's backwards: the lifted tack is the one to stay on. Race 3 is the clearest case: all three wind-call tacks were on lifts of 5–8°. Next time: the trimmer calls the compass number every 30 s on each tack. Tack when it's 5° worse than the beat's average, not before.
  2. The right side every time. Every beat was sailed 70–100% right of the rhumb line. That's fine when the wind is drifting right, as it did by 4–5° in race 1. But on race 2's second beat the wind went 9° left and we were still 94% on the right. Next time: decide the side from the wind before the beat, and make "going right" a call you make each time, not a habit.
  3. Tack losses. 31–37% speed loss per tack, worse than Sunday, and race 3's tacks took 21 s to recover (13 m lost each). Next time: slower helm in the lighter air; hold the jib until the bow is through, then trim hard.

Race 1 is the model: the two tacks with a real shift behind them were both on headers, and none were on lifts. Shift calls under 3–4° are soft, because a puff that lets us point higher reads as a lift. We sailed headed by 5° or more without tacking only once all day (48 s, race 2 first beat).

Data notes: these courses had no marks in Njord, so legs were detected from heel and the finish from the line crossing. Speeds are over ground. Wind speed is your 8–10 kt; wind direction is estimated from tacking headings. No other boats were tracked.

One question: what was the thinking behind going right on every beat: pressure, current off the Point, or the fleet? That changes whether pattern 2 is a mistake or a plan.
